content.title: About
content.content: Brussels sprouts are small cabbage-like vegetables belonging to the cruciferous family. Fresh, cooked without added fat, they retain a crisp texture and a mildly nutty flavor. The vegetable is commonly used in side dishes, salads, and soups.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name comes from Brussels, Belgium, where the vegetable was first cultivated on a large scale in the 16th century.
Each sprout is actually a miniature bud composed of many tightly packed leaves.
They are rich in glucoraphanin, a type of fiber that supports gut health.
There are over 300 varieties differing in size, leaf color, and taste.
When stored properly in the refrigerator, sprouts stay fresh for 2–3 weeks.

items.title: High in vitamin C
items.content: One cup of cooked Brussels sprouts provides more than 100 % of the daily vitamin C requirement, which supports immunity and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Source of folate
items.content: Folate is needed for cell division and is especially important for pregnant women.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: The sprouts contain quercetin and kaempferol, antioxidants that help combat free radicals.

items.title: High dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and contributes to a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Cruciferous vegetables can cause increased gas production in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Interaction with blood thinners
items.content: Large amounts of vitamin K may affect the efficacy of anticoagulant medications.

items.title: Digestive difficulty for young children
items.content: Small sprouts can be hard for young children to digest; it is advisable to finely chop them.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Brussels sprouts can be eaten raw in salads, steamed, boiled, or sautéed without added fat (e.g., in a microwave). Steaming preserves most vitamins. A squeeze of lemon juice or a pinch of spices can enhance flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store sprouts in the refrigerator in a plastic bag or container, where they stay fresh for up to 2 weeks. Do not wash before storing to avoid excess moisture.
